summary: #320 priority: can primitive thisness distinguish two unrestricted pure acts? Related/context lookup reused PartFreePlurality, RootMultiplication (#697 fork) and the Joint single-mover carrier. Their represented essence map cannot ask whether a thisness is something in the being, so a typed real-determination interface (Has, Pure) was added. Unrestricted perfection plus strict pure actuality constructively leave only bare plurality (pureActPluralityIsBare); a real thisness is then a pure perfection and is shared (thisnessIsPure, uniqueFromRealThisness); identity of real indiscernibles excludes bare plurality (uniqueFromRealIndividuation). Controls: the unchanged part-free model is the bare rival; non-pure thisness (Scotist-shaped) fails only strict purity; thisness counted pure fails only unrestricted perfection (ordinary immaterial simplicity); identity of real indiscernibles exceeds uniqueness; real thisness is not an equivalent of uniqueness; positive witness. Both uniqueness bundles are inclusion-minimal in this profile. Rejected: letting Has contain identity predicates (trivializes individuation); reading the existing formal-or-eminent every-perfection as real possession of every determination; deriving strict purity from absence of potency. All four results zero-axiom and Comparator/NanoDa accepted locally. frontier-diff: no change. FOLLOW-UP 2026-11-07: narrower bridge PurelyDeterminedIndiscerniblesIdentical (bare difference needs a non-pure determination in one of the two beings). It suffices with the two pure-act premises (uniqueFromPureIndiscernibility; three omission controls), is strictly weaker than identity of real indiscernibles (registered strengthens; strict on a Black-style carrier where located non-first beings are barely distinct), and fails with determination-free inert rows. Renaming test: if only first movers are purely determined, then under the two pure-act premises it is equivalent to at-most-one, so it supports uniqueness only if defended as a general principle about numerical difference. All three results zero-axiom, Comparator/NanoDa accepted locally; frontier-diff no change. Necessary-root connection (2026-11-07): the three pure-act premises restated for actual roots of the selected grounding relation (separate statements; actual rootness is not first-mover status) give STMT-UNIQUE-NECESSARY-ACTUAL-ROOT together with the four whole-roster existence premises, by re-indexing the first-mover theorems (firstIffRoot) rather than restating them; the narrower bridge works the same way. This is a second uniqueness route to the necessary-root endpoint, disjoint from the maximum-in-being bundle apart from the shared existence premises. Omission controls on one-world profiles: bare roots, non-pure and pure thisnesses, and an empty carrier each break uniqueness; one-root positive witness.
blocker: Bare numerical difference among purely determined beings survives without the narrower bridge. Its defense must be a general account of numerical difference (required frame of multiplicity versus merely accompanying frame); under the natural background that only first movers are purely determined, no independent test case distinguishes the answers, so this is a judgment that cannot yet be encoded. Strict pure actuality and unrestricted perfection over real determinations remain open; they now reach the necessary-root endpoint only in their root-indexed form, and no bridge identifies actual roots with first movers.
